newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Italy govt seeks confidence vote on milk.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Italy govt seeks confidence vote on milk.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government intends to call a vote of confidence in the Senate to ram through a decree to reform the milk sector, a minister said.
Minister for Relations with Parliament Giorgio Bogi announced the decision at a meeting of Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition partners.
The debate was expected to begin later on Tuesday after the government formally called the vote. The vote was expected to be held on Wednesday.
Prodi, who controls a clear majority in the Senate (upper house), won a similar do-or-die motion in the Chamber of Deputies last week.
The decree bill relates to a package of reforms for the dairy sector, which has been hit by a bitter dispute with farmers over strict European Union quotas.
Prodi's government unveiled the decree, containing emergency aid measures, in January after farmers blockaded roads and airports for two weeks to protest against hefty EU overproduction fines.
The farmers had accused the government of failing to advise them of their correct quotas and initially refused to pay.
The government responded with the bill, which offered cheap loans, payments of fines by instalment and a pledge to set up a commission to examine the farmers' grievances.
Italy has also asked the European Commission to increase its milk quotas.

The European Commission decided earlier this month to withhold farm funds due to Italy, Spain and Greece for failing to pay the so-called EU super-levy fines for overshooting their strict 1995-96 milk output quotas.
Italian farmers were fined 192.2 million Ecus ($167 million). They have already made a partial payment.
Agriculture Minister Michele Pinto survived a no-confidence vote last month after opposition parties tried to oust him for his handling of the crisis.
Decree laws issued by the government have force for only 60 days unless approved within that time by the parliament.
They cannot be re-issued and Prodi has called several confidence votes to push through legislation. He has survived them all comfortably. The milk decree expires on April 1.
